- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day forecast (e.g., day 1–5), especially when sentiment is neutral or negative; add 0.5–1.5% bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2), model lags in adjusting; delay peak forecast by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude by 1–2%.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts stay above 80% of 30-day moving average for 5+ days; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with historical volatility.
